gaps.note: Every ANSI-valid LT card the coverage grid lists is modelled and accepted in these slots, except FELT-B AC (3FE69486AC), for which no data sheet exists in any staged document. FELT-C is an ETSI/MII card and is not accepted by this ANSI shelf. The copper DSL/POTS cards (NDLS, NPOT, NIAT, NDPS, NVPS) are out of scope by decision (roc-ops/Portrayal#538).

airflow.note: HIM R6.9 s5.2 requires the FX-16 heat and fiber baffle kit and drip tray in a vertical-mount installation for NEBS preferred airflow, which it describes as front-in, rear-out; the fan tray sits under the cage. The path through the shelf itself is not stated in any staged document, so no airflow is declared.

breakers-not-bays.note: The breakers, lamps and button are fixed parts of the PDBP-C, which is built into the ANSI shelf and is not an FRU (the coverage grid: "part number never given; no own UDS"). No breaker component exists in std/ or common/, so each breaker is panel decor - bezel, toggle and handle - and not a placement; the lamps, the ACO button, the ESD point, the craft port, the ToD jack and the screws are common/std parts.

chassis.note: 3HH90279AAAATQZZA23 s3.5.2: width 499.4 mm, overall over flanges 529.4, mounting centre distance 515, depth 280, depth from rack mounting plane 246.6, height 622.5; s3.5.3 weight 14.5 kg without the fan tray. The data sheet 3FE65209BAAATQZZA04/A05 s1.6.2 prints width 497.4 and a mounting centre of 566.7 (larger than the 529.4 flanges, so a misprint). 499.4 is modelled: the drawing itself decides it - its flange-hole centres measure 513.4 apart against the 515 stated (0.3 percent) at the 499.4 scale and 511.3 (0.7 percent) at the 497.4 scale, and its x and y px/mm agree to 0.17 percent at 499.4 against 0.24 at 497.4. The body modelled is the metal between the flange folds; the flanges (ears) are not drawn, per the method; the drawing puts them at 15.7 mm a side, the stated figures at (529.4 - 499.4) / 2 = 15.

columns.note: Stated pitches (UDS s3.4.1 "NT cards: 30 mm, NT I/O card: 25 mm, LT cards: 25 mm") placed on what the drawing shows. The NT block is centred on the body to 0.1 mm (NT A, NTIO and NT B backplane connectors at 221.5 / 249.7 / 276.9 against 222.2 / 249.7 / 277.2 for 30-25-30 about the 249.7 centre), so it runs 207.2 to 292.2. The LT blocks do NOT abut it: the drawing draws a wall between LT8 and NT A and between NT B and LT9, and three independent series agree that each LT block sits about 3 mm out from the NT block - the slot legends (LT1 17.3, LT8 192.7, LT9 308.8, LT16 482.5, mirror-symmetric about 249.9), the LT backplane connectors (a constant 1.4 mm left of slot centre in both blocks) and the card-guide tabs on the top rail (a constant 2.3 mm right of each slot's left edge in both blocks). LT1-8 are therefore modelled from 4.2 to 204.2 and LT9-16 from 295.2 to 495.2, leaving 3.0 walls and 4.2 side walls; every legend and connector then lands within 1.1 mm of its slot centre. The drawn LT pitch is 24.92 (0.3 percent short of 25); the stated pitch is held. The wall width is derived, not stated.

connector-band.note: Figure 13 and UDS Figure 13 (the 3D callout art, p51) with Table 9 items 1-8. Craft port DB-9 shell 19.5-48.8 x 587.2-598.1 with jackscrews at 21.65 and 46.65 (25.0 apart, the DB-9 spacing), in a printed box 17.1-51.3 x 571.2-600.9 captioned CRAFT PORT - the "bottom left side" HIM s6.9 names. Power terminals: four dual-post terminals whose studs sit on a line at 30.2 degrees, 15.9 apart (the 5/8 in dual-hole lug spacing), stud centres (108.7, 592.7) and (122.45, 584.7) for TB1-1 and repeating every 58.95 across; the angled shrouds that carry them and their legends TB1-1 -48V BAT A, TB1-2 BAT RTN A, TB1-3 BAT RTN B, TB1-4 -48V BAT B are traced as printed outlines. Alarm plate 348.1-474.9 x 570.4-607.3: six wire-wrap pins in two columns at 357.45 and 369.5, rows 586.7 / 592.65 / 598.65, captioned NT-A, NT-B and RING / TIP / FRAME GND (UDS Table 14: X225-X230, NTB and NTA ring and tip plus two frame grounds); the ToD/1 Hz RJ-45 (Table 15) at 392.0, 592.7 under 1 Hz-PULSE; the 50-pin micro D-sub CO alarm connector (Table 16) shell 425.5-461.3 x 589.3-596.1 in a 53.6 mm flange, under CO ALARMS. The drawing prints TIME OF DAY above 1 Hz-PULSE, but its upper half is behind the fan tray's lower lip in the elevation and it is not transcribed; NT-A and NT-B are visible and are.

defaults.note: The default build is one FANT-H BB in NT A, the NT dummy in NT B, the dummy in NTIO and in all sixteen LT slots, and the BFAN-H. A shelf is never shipped with open slots - the dummies exist for airflow and EMC - and FANT-H BB is the current ANSI NT.

fan-bay.note: nokia/bfan-h@1 is 493.4 wide (UDS s35.5.1); the body is 499.4, so the tray is centred at x 3.0. The drawing's side walls step in to 5.4 and 494.1 at the fan level (opening 488.7), so the tray's last 2.4 mm each side run behind the wall lips - a 1 percent disagreement between the stated width and the drawn opening, noted rather than resolved.

fan-cover.note: Whose is the fan cover? HIM R6.9 Procedure 13 (p101): "Loosen the captive screws of the fan cover and remove the cover" (Figure 40), then "Pull the unit out of the fan area by the handles" (Figure 41, the bare tray, handle recessed in its side), then "Replace the fan unit cover". The FX-16 parts list (s5.2.2) names the shelf and "one fan unit (BFAN-H)" and no cover, and UDS Table 13 lists the ALM lamp under "Fan unit area front panel LED" in the SHELF chapter. No staged document gives the cover a part number or says which item ships it. The BFAN-H's own data sheet (3FE66546AAAATQZZA03 Figure 2) draws the tray's front with the cover on, which is why nokia/bfan-h already draws that face and why no separate cover is placed here: the bay seats the tray and the tray brings its front. BUT the three drawings disagree about that front - see the gap fan-front: this shelf elevation and HIM Figure 40 put the ALM lamp about 127 mm from the cover's left end, and the BFAN-H data sheet at mid-width, 246.4.

ground.note: HIM R6.9 s6.3.1: "the 7360 ISAM FX-16 includes two grounding cable connectors. Each ground lug is a 4 AWG, 1/4 in. stud with 1 in. hole spacing" dual-hole lug; Figure 42 (p107) places them on the left and the right side at the bottom front. The side elevation in 3FE65209BAAATQZZA04 Figure 13 (drawn with the front at its right, so the LEFT side) draws the stud pair at 210.5 and 235.85 from the rear (25.35 apart, the 1 in spacing), 586.85 down, at the same 6.2619 px/mm. The right-side pair is modelled as its mirror (56.8 from the front); Figure 42's close-up shows it there but in perspective. EACH CONNECTOR IS ONE PAIR (#828, #830): common/ground-stud-pair-1-1-4@1, two 1/4 in. (1/4-20) pan-head screws at exactly 25.4, the stud-pair-1 interface's pitch, side by side and centred on the drawn pair's midpoint (223.175 from the rear on the left side, 56.8 from the front on the right), so the screws land at 210.475 and 235.875, within 0.03 of the drawing. Formerly one common/ground-lug@1 turned 90 for the whole pair. A two-hole lug seated on a pair leaves its wire to the right of the view: toward the front on the left side, toward the rear on the right side; on the hardware that is the installer's choice (#829).

ground-stud-size.note: HIM R6.9 s6.3.1 gives each of the two grounding cable connectors of the FX-16 as a 1/4 in. stud with 1 in. hole spacing, for a 4 AWG dual-hole lug: the `stud-size` of ground-left and ground-right, each of which is one pair of studs.

model.note: 3HH90279AAAATQZZA23 Table 8: 3FE 65209 BA, mnemonic NFXS-D, "FX-16 shelf for ANSI". The data sheet 3FE65209BAAATQZZA04 is headed "NFXS-D - 7360 ISAM FX-16 Shelf - version D" and its figure is the one the UDS reprints, so both describe the same BA build.

nt-occupants.note: The slotmap and coverage grid list FANT-F, FANT-G, FANT-H (AA, BA, BB) and FANT-M as NT boards for the FX-16. Of those modelled for ANSI: FANT-H BB (UDS s20.3 "can be used in a Lightspan FX shelf") and FANT-M BA/BB (UDS s24, Figure 105 "Position of the FANT-M BA in a Lightspan FX-16 shelf") are accepted. FANT-H BC is NOT: UDS s21.3 "can be used in a Lightspan FX (FX-8 and FX-4 only) shelf". The ANSI FANT-F (BC/BD/BF, nokia/fant-f-bd@1) and FANT-G BA (nokia/fant-g-ba@1), which the coverage grid places in FX-16/8/4/12, are accepted. The ETSI builds (FANT-H AA/AC, nokia/fant-m-etsi@1) belong to the ETSI shelves. The NT dummy 3FE65651AA closes NT B when a single NT is fitted, as on every FX shelf.

ntio-occupants.note: The slotmap lists FNIO-A/B/D/E for the FX-16; all four are modelled and accepted. The LT/NTIO dummy 3FE65651BA closes the slot when no NT I/O card is fitted.

panel-scale.note: Gate 1. Figure 13 rendered at 1200 dpi: the body is 3122 px between the outer edges of its side walls and 3898 px from the top plate's outer edge to the bottom edge (the card-guide tabs stand 5 mm above the top plate and are outside the 622.5). 3122 / 499.4 = 6.2515 px/mm across, 3898 / 622.5 = 6.2619 down, 0.17 percent apart; the flange extent, 3318 px over 529.4, gives 6.268. So the figure is orthographic and every position below is a measurement at about 0.16 mm/px, read by connected-component extraction of each feature's box, limited in practice by the drawing's 0.5 to 3 mm stroke widths. The UDS Figure 22 raster (150 ppi) is the same art and was used only to confirm that.

power.note: The shelf itself draws nothing: every consumer is a card with its own `power-draw-max-w` and the fan tray's (nokia/bfan-h: 315 W at full speed). The PDBP-C takes two -48 V feeds through the TB1 terminals and protects each with a dual-pole breaker, 2 x 35 A = 70 A per branch (UDS s3.4.5.6); the voltage-monitor thresholds are in s3.4.5.4. No shelf-level power envelope is stated in any staged document; searched the UDS chapter 3, HIM R6.9 chapter 6 and the coverage grid, whose power column reads "n/a".

terminal-cover.note: UDS Figure 20 (p61) and HIM Figures 45 and 47 show a safety cover, labelled "CAUTION: BEFORE REMOVING TERMINAL COVER, DISCONNECT BOTH A AND B POWER SOURCES", that closes over the four terminals once cabled.
